items.title:
io.youtrackdb:youtrackdb-embedded 0.5.0-beta-2026-10-24 发布, Uber-jar with all third-party dependencies relocated under
    com.jetbrains.youtrackdb.shade to avoid classpath conflicts
    when YouTrackDB is used as an embedded library.

    NOTE: The custom TinkerPop fork (io.youtrackdb:gremlin-*) retains
    the org.apache.tinkerpop Java package and is intentionally NOT
    relocated. Relocating it would break ServiceLoader entries, Gremlin
    plugin registrations, and reflection-based lookups. Users who also
    depend on upstream Apache TinkerPop should use dependency exclusions.

    Netty, SLF4J, and GraalVM/Truffle are excluded from the uber-jar
    (not bundled) and must be provided by the user:
    - Netty: native transport relies on class-path-relative resource loading.
    - SLF4J: logging facade whose binding must be chosen by the user.
    - GraalVM/Truffle: internal class loading by name; needed only if the
      Gremlin JavaScript engine is used.
    The shaded jar is unsigned (original signatures are stripped during
    repackaging).

    Netty, SLF4J, and GraalVM/Truffle are excluded from the uber-jar
    (not bundled) and must be provided by the user:
    - Netty: native transport relies on class-path-relative resource loading.
    - SLF4J: logging facade whose binding must be chosen by the user.
    - GraalVM/Truffle: internal class loading by name; needed only if the
      Gremlin JavaScript engine is used.
    The shaded jar is unsigned (original signatures are stripped during
    repackaging).

se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations 1.4.1 发布, VibeTags annotation classes (@AILocked, @AIContext, @AIDraft, @AIAudit,
        @AIIgnore, @AIPrivacy, @AICore, @AIPerformance). Zero third-party dependencies.
        All annotations use RetentionPolicy.SOURCE so they leave no trace in the
        consumer's compiled bytecode — this jar exists purely to give javac the
        symbols it needs at compile time.

        Pair this with vibetags-processor on the annotation-processor classpath:

        Maven:
            <dependency>
                <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
                <artifactId>vibetags-annotations</artifactId>
                <version>1.4.1</version>
            </dependency>

        Gradle:
            compileOnly 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations:1.4.1'
            annotationProcessor 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-processor:1.4.1'

se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom 1.4.1 发布, Bill of Materials for the VibeTags annotation processor. Import this BOM to get
        a coherent vibetags-annotations + vibetags-processor pair without specifying
        each version individually.

        Recommended setup — annotations on the compile classpath, processor on the
        annotation-processor path only (the processor jar pulls in slf4j/logback,
        which has no business on consumer code's compileClasspath):

        Maven:
            <dependencyManagement>
                <dependencies>
                    <dependency>
                        <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
                        <artifactId>vibetags-bom</artifactId>
                        <version>1.4.1</version>
                        <type>pom</type>
                        <scope>import</scope>
                    </dependency>
                </dependencies>
            </dependencyManagement>

        Gradle:
            implementation platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.4.1')
            annotationProcessor platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.4.1')
            compileOnly 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations'
            annotationProcessor 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-processor'

        Kotlin with KSP instead of kapt (vibetags-ksp in place of the processor):
            implementation(platform("se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.4.1"))
            ksp(platform("se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.4.1"))
            compileOnly("se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations")
            ksp("se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-ksp")

se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-cli 1.4.1 发布, Companion command-line tool for VibeTags: `init` bootstraps a project's opt-in
        files (file presence is the opt-in signal the processor honours), `doctor`
        reports the project's VibeTags health — build-tool wiring, active platforms,
        marker integrity. Run it without installing anything:

            jbang se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-cli:1.4.1 init --list

        The platform list and marker rules are read from vibetags-processor, so this
        tool cannot drift from what the processor actually does.
